sentences.text: Liaoningopterus was a large pterosaur with an estimated skull length of 61 cm and a wingspan of 5 meters.
It possessed a symmetrical snout crest measuring 12 cm in length and 17 mm in height, alongside a fourth upper jaw tooth reaching 81 mm.
The animal had an estimated body mass of 20 kg.
Its 81 mm tooth represents the largest known tooth length for any pterosaur.
The creature featured a symmetrical snout crest, a structure that was 12 cm long.
The genus Liaoningopterus was named in 2003 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe, with the type species designated as Liaoningopterus gui.
Researchers described Liaoningopterus as probably a piscivore due to its long, pointed snout.
Wang classified Liaoningopterus as a member of the Anhangueridae family primarily due to its crests, while a 2006 cladistic analysis by Lü Junchang showed it to be a basal member of that same group.

A 2008 analysis by Ji Qiang placed Liaoningopterus in a trichotomy with Anhanguera and Tropeognathus, whereas under David Unwin's alternative terminology, the animal is considered a member of the Ornithocheiridae.
The parent group of Liaoningopterus is Ornithocheiroidea.
Liaoningopterus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
